newsitem.title: USA: Sears Q4 uncollectibles rise to $328 million.
newsitem.headline: Sears Q4 uncollectibles rise to $328 million.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co said Thursday its provision for uncollectible accounts rose in the 1996 fourth quarter and the company has implemented some measures to improve collection efforts.
Sears said its provision for uncollectible accounts increased by $133 million to $328 million in the 1996 fourth quarter, largely due to a 56.9 percent increase in account charge-offs.
The charge-offs reflect continuing growth in its credit receivable portfolio as well as an industry-wide increase in personal bankruptcies and delinquencies, the retailer said.

"Credit continued its strong performance despite increased uncollectibles," said Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Arthur Martinez. He added that the company "has a number of initiatives already in place to improve collection efforts, including increased staffing and investments in technology."
Sears domestic credit portfolio, which consists primarily of Sears Card customer receivables, continued to perform well in 1996, he said in statement.
Credit revenues increased by 17.2 percent in the fourth quarter due to higher receivable balances driven by strong merchandise sales and uniform pricing.
The increase in credit revenues, coupled with reduced funding rates, improved the fourth quarter net interest margin by $160 million, Sears said.
Earlier Thursday, Sears reported its 1996 fourth-quarter income rose 24.6 percent to $567 million or $1.42 a share from $455 million or $1.13 in fourth-quarter 1995.

The double-digit income growth was achieved on a 10.8 percent increase in fourth-quarter 1996 revenues, which rose to $12.04 billion from $10.87 billion in fourth-quarter 1995, the retailer said in a year-end financial statement.
